key_insight: A multimodal pretreatment biomarker signature predicted primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced NSCLC better than PD-L1 or TMB alone.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help identify patients unlikely to benefit from standard anti-PD-(L)1 regimens before treatment starts.
method: Prospective multicentre study in 439 patients with advanced NSCLC across 17 centres.
Collected six pretreatment data layers: clinical, routine labs, immune phenotyping, soluble markers, digital pathology, transcriptomics, and genomics.
Benchmarked 36 feature-selection methods and 10 machine-learning models under a .632 optimism-correction framework.
evidence_signal: The best multimodal model reached an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.73±0.05 and PPV of 0.63±0.07 overall, outperforming PD-L1 and TMB.
watch_item: The signature is complex and needs external validation and practical workflow testing before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Multimodal profiling for prediction of primary resistance to anti-PD-(L)1 therapy in advanced non-small-cell lung cancer: the prospective PIONeeR biomarkers study
